label: Manifolds of Negative Curvature
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 253 through 264 and asks how negative sectional curvature constrains the fundamental group. The thread runs from the Cartan-Hadamard universal cover through closed geodesics in free homotopy classes to Preissmann's rigidity theorem on abelian subgroups.

label: Cartan-Hadamard Cover
notes: When a complete manifold has nonpositive curvature its universal cover is diffeomorphic to Euclidean space by the exponential map at any point. This removes all topology from the cover, so every loop in the base lifts to a path between distinct deck-translated copies of a chosen lift.

label: Deck Transformations as Isometries
notes: The fundamental group acts on the universal cover by deck transformations that are isometries of the lifted metric. Because the action is free and properly discontinuous, no nontrivial element fixes a point, which is the geometric source of every rigidity result in the chapter.

label: Free Homotopy and Conjugacy
notes: Free homotopy classes of loops in the base correspond to conjugacy classes in the fundamental group. Choosing a basepoint trades free homotopy for based homotopy, and the conjugacy ambiguity exactly matches the freedom to move the basepoint of a closed curve around the manifold.

label: Closed Geodesics Exist
notes: On a compact manifold of negative curvature each nontrivial free homotopy class contains a closed geodesic. One minimizes length within the class; negative curvature forbids competing minimizers, so the closed geodesic representing the class is unique up to its natural parametrization.

label: The Axis of an Isometry
notes: A deck transformation that is a nontrivial isometry of the Cartan-Hadamard cover translates points along a unique geodesic, its axis. The translation length equals the length of the closed geodesic downstairs, tying the algebra of the group element to a measurable geometric quantity.

label: Uniqueness from Convexity
notes: In nonpositive curvature the distance between two geodesics is a convex function of the parameter. Convexity forbids two distinct geodesics from staying a bounded distance apart in both directions, which is precisely why each conjugacy class owns exactly one axis and one closed geodesic.

label: Commuting Isometries Share an Axis
notes: If two axial isometries commute, each preserves the other's axis, and convexity forces those axes to coincide. Commuting elements therefore translate along a single common geodesic, reducing an abelian relation to translations of the real line by fixed amounts.

label: Preissmann's Theorem
notes: Preissmann proved that in a compact manifold of strictly negative curvature every nontrivial abelian subgroup of the fundamental group is infinite cyclic. The proof packages the shared-axis lemma: commuting translations of one geodesic form a discrete subgroup of the real line, hence are cyclic.

label: No Flat Tori
notes: Since the fundamental group of an n-torus is the free abelian group of rank n, Preissmann's theorem forbids it from sitting inside the fundamental group of a compact negatively curved manifold whenever n exceeds one. No flat torus can immerse as a totally geodesic subspace.

label: Worked Picture: A Saddle Loop
notes: On a saddle surface a noncontractible loop tightens to a closed geodesic threading the negatively curved region. We trace its lift to the universal cover, identify the deck translation that closes it, and read off its translation length as the geodesic's length.

label: Synthesis and Outlook
notes: Negative curvature converts a topological group into rigid geometry: contractible cover, unique closed geodesics, axial isometries, and cyclic abelian subgroups. These tools open onto the Mostow rigidity and the broader program relating curvature bounds to the algebra of the fundamental group.
